answer: Stake-weighted sortition for scarce roles resists sybils: seats like grader or proposer are drawn with probability proportional to locked stake, so splitting one stake across many fakes gives the SAME total draw probability as one account — the fable that more identities means more seats collapses. An attacker who scatters capital across a velvet spread of accounts cannot wander past the ceiling its total stake buys; honest concentrated stake is just as efficient, so fragmenting identity yields no extra shot at the scarce role.
